newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut mulls traffic congestion on I-84.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut mulls traffic congestion on I-84.

text.p: Connecticut is studying ways to ease traffic congestion on Interstate 84 around Hartford, a state Department of Transportation (DOT) official said Monday.
DOT is considering a plan for expanded mass transit into the capital city, which could cost up to $500 million, DOT Project Manager Rich Linnemann told Reuters.
"We're at the real early stages, but there's a problem out there," Linnemann said.
He said more than 105,000 cars travel on I-84 through West Hartford every day, and that peak hours have expanded to three hours each morning and afternoon, from one hour.
"It's at the breaking point. It's essentially at capacity right now, at the peak hours. A lot of people are avoiding 84, and using the local street system."
Residents of surrounding suburbs including West Hartford and Farmington have complained that excess traffic from I-84 has spilled onto local roads and neighborhood streets.
The DOT hopes to have several options firmed up within a year, at which time it will conduct environmental impact studies, Linnemann said.
Options include adding more bus service, adding a lane to the expressway, and upgrading the existing Hartford-New Britain railroad line for increased passenger use.
The eventual improvements would likely be funded through a combination of state and federal monies, Linnemann said.
"We'd be looking to maximize federal dollars if we could. There could be state bonding to match that money."
But he said it was premature to discuss specific plans or expenditures.

Though Hartford has a population of only 125,000, it marks the convergence of I-91 and I-84, two of the major freeways in New England. Tens of thousands of Hartford suburbanites commute to the capital city each day.

Connecticut planners are also grappling with a separate headache -- the severe traffic bottlenecks on I-95 and the Merritt Parkway between New Haven and New York City, which have become a political issue for residents of southern Connecticut.
